full_judgment: 8. We have examined the evidence on record. The original title Suit No. 80 of 1993 was renumbered as Title Suit No. 75 of 1994 by order No. 8 dated 16.7.94 in the 2nd Court Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah. Ext. 1 is the khas Ammokternama in 5 sheets admitted into evidence without any objection. Ext. 1(A) is the disputed power of attorney dated 26.9.62 also admitted into evidence without raising any objection by the defendant appellants at the time of trail. In view of the case law reported in 22 D.L.R. page 858 Sadequr Rahman Chowdhury Vs. Mvi. Abdul Bari, the defendant appellants cannot raise any objection at the time of appeal hearing regarding the disputed power of attorney when the contesting defendants raised no objection against the same disputed power of attorney dated 26.9.62 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah when it was admitted into evidence and marked Ext. 1(A). Moreover, the disputed power of attorney is authenticated by the Deputy Commissioner, Jessore with a certificate that the general power of attorney has been duly stamped and the power of attorney is attested by A.B. Mokherjee Notary Public, Calcutta and counter signed by the then Deputy High Commissioner of Pakistan in Calcutta and it bears the official seal of the Deputy High Commissioner. The Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah rightly observed in the impugned judgment that the presumptive value under section 85 of the Evidence Act is applicable to this disputed power of attorney. The disputed power of attorney was executed on 26.9.62. The East Pakistan Disturbed Persons (Rehabilitation) Ordinance No. 1/1964 was made effective from 30th June, 1964, hence the legal bar mentioned in section 4 and section 6 of Ordinance No. 1 of 1964 is not applicable to the instant power of attorney dated 26.9.62 marked Ext. 1 (A). In this connection the trial Court rightly cited a case law reported in 17 D.L.R. page 451, Chitta Ranjan Sutar Vs. Secretary, Judicial Department, Government of East Pakistan that section 4 and 6 of the Ordinance No. 1 of 1964 place unreasonable restrictions on the right of a citizen to acquire property and the same is violative of the fundamental right 13th and as such they are void and are also discriminatory under Fundamental right 15th.
